### Problem: Third Maximum Number {#sec-arr-p1-a}

::: {.p-statement}
Given a **non-empty** array $a$ of integers ($1 \le n \le 10^4$, $-2^{31} \le a_i \le 2^{31}-1$), return the **third** largest *distinct* value. If fewer than three distinct values exist, return the largest. Example: $[2, 2, 3, 1] \to 1$, because the distinct values are $3 > 2 > 1$. Aim for $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ space.

Source: [LC 414 · Third Maximum Number](https://leetcode.com/problems/third-maximum-number/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
You never need the array sorted — only the three best *distinct* values. Keep them in three variables and slide them down the ranks as you meet something bigger, skipping anything already among them.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Brute force.** Sort a copy, deduplicate, take index $-3$ (or the last if only $1$–$2$ remain): $O(n\log n)$ time, $O(n)$ space.
2. **One pass, $O(1)$ space.** Track `first > second > third` (or `None` = not yet filled). For each $x$: skip if $x$ already equals one of them; otherwise slot $x$ in from the top. At the end return `third` if it exists, else `first`.

**Invariant.** After processing $[0,i)$, `first, second, third` are the three largest distinct values in that range, in order.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Sort, dedupe, take the third

::: {.form-next}
Read the definition literally: sort a copy, drop duplicates, and the answer is the third from the right (or the last, if fewer than three distinct values survive). Simple and provably right, at $O(n\log n)$ time and $O(n)$ space — more work than the problem needs.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def third_max_brute(a):
    d = sorted(set(a))
    return d[-3] if len(d) >= 3 else d[-1]
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <algorithm>
using namespace std;

int thirdMaxBrute(vector<int> nums) {
    sort(nums.begin(), nums.end());
    nums.erase(unique(nums.begin(), nums.end()), nums.end());
    return nums.size() >= 3 ? nums[nums.size() - 3] : nums.back();
}
```
:::

#### Slide three slots in one pass

::: {.form-next}
You never need the array sorted — only the three best *distinct* values. Keep `first > second > third` in three variables and slide them down the ranks when something bigger appears, skipping any value already among them. One pass, $O(1)$ space; return `third` if it filled, else `first`.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("third", "slide")
    assert str(final) == "1"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: arr-third-max
def third_max(a: list[int]) -> int:
    first = second = third = None
    for x in a:
        if x in (first, second, third):
            continue
        if first is None or x > first:
            third, second, first = second, first, x
        elif second is None or x > second:
            third, second = second, x
        elif third is None or x > third:
            third = x
    return first if third is None else third


for _ in range(2000):
    a = [random.randint(-12, 12) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 12))]
    assert third_max(a) == third_max_brute(a)

assert third_max([3, 2, 1]) == 1
assert third_max([1, 2]) == 2
assert third_max([2, 2, 3, 1]) == 1    # the board sample
print("third_max OK")
```

##### C++

```cpp
#include <vector>
#include <climits>
using namespace std;

int thirdMax(vector<int>& nums) {
    long long first = LLONG_MIN, second = LLONG_MIN, third = LLONG_MIN;
    for (long long x : nums) {
        if (x == first || x == second || x == third) continue;
        if (x > first)       { third = second; second = first; first = x; }
        else if (x > second) { third = second; second = x; }
        else if (x > third)  { third = x; }
    }
    return third == LLONG_MIN ? (int)first : (int)third;
}
```
:::
:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Sort, dedupe, take the third** is $O(n\log n)$ time and $O(n)$ space. **Slide three slots in one pass** is $O(n)$ time and $O(1)$ space: one pass, a constant number of comparisons per element, three variables regardless of $n$ or the value range. (Using `LLONG_MIN` as a sentinel is safe because inputs are `int`, so no real value equals it.)
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Fewer than three distinct values (including all equal) $\to$ return the maximum.
- Duplicates must not consume a rank: the `x in (first, second, third)` skip is the whole point.
- Negatives and $-2^{31}$: the sentinel must be strictly below `int`'s range, hence `long long`. With `INT_MIN` as the sentinel, $[1, 2, -2^{31}]$ would report "no third value" and return $2$ instead of $-2^{31}$.
:::
